c.tagline: Beer gardens, baroque spires, and Alpine air

emergency.note: 112 works EU-wide for fire and ambulance; English-speaking operators are common.

hood_landmark.Altstadt: Marienplatz and the Neues Rathaus Glockenspiel
hood_landmark.Schwabing: the Englischer Garten's meadows, surfers and beer gardens
hood_landmark.Maxvorstadt: the Kunstareal's three Pinakothek art museums
hood_landmark.Haidhausen: Wiener Platz's market stalls and historic Hofbräukeller beer garden
hood_landmark.Glockenbachviertel: Gärtnerplatz square and its ornate Gärtnerplatztheater

avoid.reason: Very safe; pickpocketing at the Hauptbahnhof and during Oktoberfest

hood_desc: Altstadt is Munich's historic old town centered on Marienplatz, packed with landmarks, beer halls and the Viktualienmarkt, ideal for first-time visitors and sightseers.
Schwabing is the elegant former artists' quarter beside the English Garden, full of cafes, boutiques and leafy streets, suited to relaxed and upmarket travelers.
Maxvorstadt is the university and museum district holding the Pinakothek galleries, with student cafes and a cultured, intellectual vibe, great for art lovers.
Haidhausen is a charming, village-like neighborhood of cobbled squares, wine bars and the Gasteig arts center, appealing to families and calmer stays.
Glockenbachviertel is Munich's trendy nightlife and LGBTQ+ district with stylish bars, design shops and riverside walks, perfect for a lively social scene.

water.note: Tap water is high quality and safe to drink straight from the tap.

transit.pay: No transit card needed: buy tickets in the MVGO or MVV app or from station machines (bank cards accepted) and validate before boarding. A zone M single is about 4 EUR (~US$4.50) and a day ticket about 10 EUR; one ticket covers U-Bahn, S-Bahn, trams and buses. The airport-city day ticket is good value for arrivals.
transit.hours: U-Bahn and S-Bahn run about 4am-1am (until ~2am on weekends); night trams and buses cover the small hours.

transit.m: S-Bahn S1 or S8 to Marienplatz (40 min)
Lufthansa Express Bus to Hauptbahnhof (45 min)

food.name: Weisswurst
food.desc: Pale veal-and-pork sausage flavoured with parsley and lemon, poached not grilled. Eaten with sweet mustard and a pretzel before noon.

places.name: Bratwurstherzl
places.note: Vaulted, wood-panelled sausage kitchen right on the market; grills over beechwood embers.

places.name: Weisses Brauhaus (Schneider)
places.note: Classic pairing of weisswurst with Schneider Weisse straight from the tap.

places.name: Wirtshaus in der Au
places.note: Local-heavy tavern known for dumplings; a short tram hop from Marienplatz.

food.name: Schweinshaxe
food.desc: Roast pork knuckle with crackling you can hear from the next table, served with a potato dumpling and dark beer gravy.

places.name: Haxnbauer
places.note: Roasts haxn over open beechwood fires in the window; the city's specialist address.

places.name: Augustiner Braeustuben
places.note: Brewery tavern where locals go for haxe and unfiltered Augustiner from wooden barrels.

places.name: Hofbraeuhaus
places.note: Touristy but genuinely enormous portions, brass band and a 400-year-old beer hall.

food.name: Obatzda
food.desc: Beer-garden spread of ripe camembert mashed with butter, paprika and a splash of beer, piled on pretzel or rye.

places.name: Chinesischer Turm
places.note: Beer garden under a wooden pagoda; buy obatzda at the self-service counter.

places.name: Viktualienmarkt Biergarten
places.note: Central beer garden where you can bring your own food from the surrounding market stalls.

places.name: Wirtshaus in der Au
places.note: House-made version with pickled onions, well matched to their own dumpling menu.

food.name: Schweinsbraten mit Knoedel
food.desc: Sunday roast pork with dark beer sauce and a bread or potato dumpling. The Bavarian dish locals order most often.

places.name: Augustiner Klosterwirt
places.note: Beside the Frauenkirche, a reliable Altstadt kitchen for roast pork and dumplings.

places.name: Zum Duernbraeu
places.note: One of the city's oldest inns, tucked in a courtyard away from the Marienplatz crowds.

places.name: Wirtshaus in der Au
places.note: Self-styled dumpling specialists; a dozen knoedel variations on the menu.

food.name: Steckerlfisch
food.desc: Whole mackerel or trout skewered on a stick, salted, and grilled over charcoal. A beer garden and Oktoberfest staple.

places.name: Koeniglicher Hirschgarten
places.note: Europe's largest beer garden, 8,000 seats under chestnuts with a dedicated fish grill.

places.name: Seehaus im Englischen Garten
places.note: Lakeside terrace on the Kleinhesseloher See, grilled fish and a long Bavarian menu.

places.name: Aumeister
places.note: Former royal hunting lodge at the park's quiet end; worth the walk or bike ride.

food.name: Schmalznudel (Auszogne)
food.desc: Hand-stretched fried dough, thin and crisp at the middle, thick at the rim, dusted with sugar. Eaten warm within minutes.

places.name: Cafe Frischhut
places.note: Known citywide as Schmalznudel; makes only four pastries and sells out early.

places.name: Rischart am Marienplatz
places.note: Long-standing Munich bakery chain with a cafe overlooking Marienplatz.

food.name: Weissbier
food.desc: Cloudy Bavarian wheat beer, banana-and-clove aromas, served in a tall vase glass. The traditional partner to weisswurst.

places.name: Weisses Brauhaus
places.note: Schneider Weisse's Munich home, pouring the original dark wheat beer since 1872.

places.name: Hofbraeuhaus
places.note: Cavernous 1589 beer hall; loud, communal, and unavoidable for a first visit.

places.name: Paulaner am Nockherberg
places.note: Big brewery tavern and beer garden, home of the strong Salvator bock each spring.

food.name: Helles by the Mass
food.desc: Pale Munich lager drunk by the litre in a stone or glass Mass. Six city breweries still supply the beer gardens.

places.name: Augustiner-Keller
places.note: 5,000 seats under chestnut trees; Augustiner Edelstoff tapped from wooden barrels.

places.name: Koeniglicher Hirschgarten
places.note: Bring your own picnic to the self-service benches and buy only the beer.

places.name: Augustiner Braeustuben
places.note: Inside the working brewery next to the horse stables; the cheapest good Mass in town.

landmarks: Marienplatz
Munich's central square, dominated by the Neo-Gothic New Town Hall and its glockenspiel, is the postcard image of the city.
Frauenkirche (Munich Cathedral)
The twin onion-domed towers of this Gothic brick cathedral form the defining silhouette of the Munich skyline.
Nymphenburg Palace
A grand Baroque summer palace with vast formal gardens, once home to Bavarian royalty and a favorite for elegant photography.
Englischer Garten (English Garden)
One of the world's largest urban parks, famous for its surfers on the Eisbach wave, beer gardens, and the Chinese Tower pagoda.
Viktualienmarkt
A lively year-round market square with a maypole and beer garden, capturing the flavor of everyday Bavarian life.
Olympiapark
The striking tent-roofed venues from the 1972 Olympics, anchored by the Olympic Tower, offer a modern architectural counterpoint to old Munich.
Munich Residenz
The former royal palace of the Wittelsbach dynasty is one of Europe's most opulent palace-museums, packed with lavish state rooms.
Hofbräuhaus am Platzl
The world-famous 16th-century beer hall is a symbol of Bavarian beer culture and one of Munich's most visited attractions.
BMW Museum / BMW Welt
The futuristic bowl-shaped museum and adjoining showroom celebrate Munich's automotive heritage with striking modern architecture.
Deutsches Museum
The world's largest science and technology museum, spread across an island in the Isar River with exhibits ranging from submarines to airplanes.

train.note: Everything leaves from Munich Hauptbahnhof, which is being rebuilt around the running railway, so allow extra time to find your platform. The overnight services are OeBB Nightjet sleepers - the Rome/Florence and Venice trains run daily, while the Amsterdam and Brussels sleepers run on selected days, so check dates. Amsterdam is also reachable by daytime ICE (~7h), and Salzburg is only 1h30 on the Railjet.

intl.to: Vienna, Prague, Zurich, Milan & across Europe

bus.note: International coaches use the ZOB central bus station at Hackerbrucke, one S-Bahn stop west of the Hauptbahnhof, a proper indoor terminal with shops and a ticket desk. Booking online is cheaper than at the counter. Prague takes about 5h30, Vienna 5h and Zurich 4h30.

ferry.note: Munich is landlocked, so there are no ferries. Local pleasure boats run on the nearby lakes (Starnberger See, Ammersee) in summer.

half.name: Neuschwanstein Castle
half.blurb: The fairytale hilltop castle that inspired Disney, set against dramatic Alpine foothills and lakes.

half.name: Salzburg
half.blurb: Mozart's baroque hometown across the border, with a hilltop fortress and Sound of Music scenery.

half.name: Dachau Memorial
half.blurb: The sobering former concentration camp, now a moving memorial and museum honoring its victims.

half.name: Zugspitze
half.blurb: Germany's highest peak, reached by cog railway and cable car for sweeping Alpine panoramas.

half.name: Konigssee
half.blurb: An emerald glacial lake ringed by soaring cliffs, explored by silent electric boats.

half.name: Nuremberg
half.blurb: A medieval walled city with an imperial castle, half-timbered lanes and rich, layered history.
